text:
maria: FYI escalating — large EU customer hitting 403 + huge latency since 03:12 UTC. They claim requests with eu residency flag are routed to us-east and audit alerts fired. Customer very upset.

sam_sre: Can you paste a sample request id + headers? Any recent deploys in routing?

maria: request_id=rid_0x9f3e, headers: 
`X-Region-Preference: eu`
`Authorization: Bearer <redacted>`
They included a snippet where response header shows `x-served-region: us-east-1`.

alex: quick look — we had a canary rollout for smart-routing fallback policy 03:05 UTC. Canary config accidentally allowed global_fallback=true for traffic type `reserved`. That can cause EU pins to go to nearest healthy pool which currently is us-east. Rolling that change out now.

tanvi: Is global_fallback a binary toggle or per-customer? We advertised per-customer pins in the console. If it's global for reserved, that's a product bug.

alex: It was meant to be per-customer, but a config template bug set the flag at pool-level during the canary. Revert in flight.

sam_sre: We need mitigation for the customer now. Options: 1) pin their tenant to eu-west-1 manually, 2) temporarily disable fallback for reserved pools, 3) set routing override at edge. Which is fastest?

support-bot: Incident playbook suggests pin via Console -> Customer -> Network -> Region Pin. ETA ~8 min if we have owner creds.

maria: Customer asked for rollback not pin. They said audit logs already show RESIDENCY_EXCEPTION and security team is filing a report.

compliance-bot: Alert: RESIDENCY_EXCEPTION detected for tenant `acme-corp` at 03:14 UTC -> thrown by routing-service v2.2. AuditID: audit_2026_03_17_0314. Policy: eu_data_residency (enforced). Exception flagged: true.

raj_billing: Heads up — we also see a billing spike for that tenant starting 03:13. Likely retries from client after 403/latency causing duplicate billable tokens. I'm seeing 3x normal token usage in a 10m window.

alex: Repro steps I ran from my laptop (no creds):
```
curl -v -H "X-Region-Preference: eu" -H "Authorization: Bearer test" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
> x-served-region: us-east-1
> x-routing-reason: fallback-pool-unavailable
```
This matches the customer's report.

sam_sre: Temporary mitigation we applied: disabled global_fallback on reserved pools at 03:18 UTC; created explicit route for tenant `acme-corp` -> eu-west-1 at 03:20 UTC. Asking edge to flush caches.

maria: Customer confirmed lower latency and 200s after 03:23. Compliance still wants a formal exception review.

compliance-bot: Logged exception for review. Required fields: root_cause, timeline, remediation, compensating controls. Please add to ticket COMP-2026-042.

alex: Root cause: config template regression during canary (global_fallback flag leaked to reserved pools). Fix: patch template, add unit test to prevent pool-level leak, add a canary gate to detect residency flag changes. Deploying patch now (target 03:45 UTC).

raj_billing: For billing noise: we can issue a one-time credit for retry window and mark usage as disputed. I'll open billing case and attach token usage graphs.

sam_sre: Postmortem owners: alex (runtime), sam_sre (infra), tanvi (product), maria (support), raj_billing (billing), compliance-bot (compliance). Action items:
- Revert canary config + verify template (alex)
- Add unit/e2e for residency flag (alex + infra)
- Temporary credit & customer comms (raj_billing + maria)
- Update console UX to show fallback status per-tenant (tanvi)
- Compliance report to COMP-2026-042 (compliance-bot)

maria: Customer asked for a written apology + assurance that audit logs will be provided. I'll deliver once comp report is ready.

support-bot: Noted. Playbook step: send initial RCA within 72 hours.

alex: Patch deployed at 03:46 UTC. Canary gate added. Running internal tests.

sam_sre: All clear from infra at 03:50 UTC — no further unexpected cross-region routes for reserved tenancy.

maria: Closing customer loop now. Will add link to COMP-2026-042 and billing case BILL-789.

compliance-bot: COMP-2026-042: status=investigating, assigned=tanvi, due=2026-03-20.

maria: Thanks team. Keeping thread open for final postmortem notes.
